answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a stake before it can trade, and the stake is slashed when peers prove fraud. A newcomer starts on a small knoll of trust, earning only tiny jobs, and must climb through verified work before reaching the zenith of high-value contracts. An identity with no history is a hollow shell — it cannot borrow the reputation of others, so spinning up thousands of cheap copies buys no access, only thousands of locked stakes that honest work would take months to earn back.
